This is the whole substance of the problem; everything else is bookkeeping. An unproved key step of this magnitude cannot be credited.", "quote": "**Proof.** Induction over the sequence terms in increasing order (standard; details omitted). $\\square$"}, {"description": "The 'surviving hypothesis' section alludes to a repair construction R p^k that is supposed to handle the boundary issue m/p < A, but this construction is never defined or used anywhere in the argument, so the gap in the lemma is not even partially filled.", "quote": "The construction \\(Rp^k\\) repairs this boundary issue while preserving exactly the small-prime support; the lemma proves the strengthened hypothesis."}, {"description": "Computational checks over 2\u2264A\u2264150 are offered in place of the missing argument. Numerical evidence earns no credit, and the text acknowledges it 'only tests' the unproved lemma.", "quote": "These computations only test the lemma; the argument above proves it independently."}], "notes": "The reduction framework (goodness, (1), upward closure, L = product of primes \u2264 a\u2081, and the deduction of a_{n+T}=a_n+L valid from n=1) is correct and cleanly written, but it is conditional on an entirely unproved lemma."}
